campaigns.hook: More than six million people beneath one city
campaigns.support: Documented history on this scale becomes folklore quickly.
campaigns.rights: Jorge Láscar via Wikimedia Commons; credit recorded on PRN case page
campaigns.facebook:
More than six million people lie beneath one city.

The Paris Catacombs began receiving human remains in 1786 after cemetery failures and dangerous quarry collapses. Later accounts describe voices, touches and footsteps underground, but the modern claims are largely anonymous and uncontrolled.

The PRN case file separates the documented history, one confirmed death and the folklore that followed: https://www.paranormalresponsenetwork.org/cases/catacombs-of-paris

#CaseArchive #LocalHistory #ResearchLed #ParanormalResponseNetwork

campaigns.hook: A black dog entered the printed record in 1577
campaigns.support: Black Shuck sits inside a much wider British phantom-dog tradition.
campaigns.facebook:
A black dog entered the printed record in 1577.

Accounts from Bungay and Blythburgh became part of the Black Shuck tradition—but East Anglia’s phantom dog is only one regional form. Barghest, Padfoot, Gytrash, Gwyllgi and Cù Sìth carry related traditions across Britain.

Explore the origins, variants and surviving sources in Kirstie’s Library: https://www.paranormalresponsenetwork.org/kirsties-library/creatures-cryptids/black-shuck-phantom-dogs

Illustrative visual.

campaigns.hook: A corridor of driver stories—not one apparition point
campaigns.support: The A75 record is testimony, road context and folklore transmission.
campaigns.rights: Ann Cook, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons; credited on PRN case page
campaigns.facebook:
The A75 story is a corridor—not one verified apparition point.

Driver accounts cluster around Carrutherstown, Kinmount and Kelhead Moss. PRN found named and anonymous reports, but no original Ferguson statement, 1997 incident file or auditable catalogue supporting the familiar “hundreds of sightings” claim.

Read the case, road context and source limitations: https://www.paranormalresponsenetwork.org/cases/a75-kinmount-straight

The A75 is an active trunk road. Do not stop or investigate.

campaigns.hook: Kaidan, yōkai and yūrei are not one category
campaigns.support: Story, image, religion and reported experience have different histories.
campaigns.rights: Historical artwork reproduced in PRN documentary archive; atmospheric context only
campaigns.facebook:
Kaidan, yōkai and yūrei are not one category.

They overlap in modern popular imagination, but their literary, visual, religious and folkloric histories are different. PRN’s Japan investigation keeps those histories apart long enough to show where they genuinely connect—and where modern English labels blur the record.

Explore the full investigation: https://www.paranormalresponsenetwork.org/global-unknown/japan-kaidan-yokai-yurei

Historical artwork documents visual tradition; it is not evidence of a verified being.

campaigns.support: Ordinary explanations, safety and privacy are reviewed first.
campaigns.facebook:
Nothing you report to PRN is published automatically.

You can describe what happened in plain language. Town-level detail is enough to begin, exact addresses stay private, and every submission is reviewed against ordinary environmental, perceptual and practical explanations first.

Read how the process works or submit an experience: https://www.paranormalresponsenetwork.org/is-it-paranormal

PRN is not an emergency service. If anyone is in immediate danger, contact local emergency services first.
